note: Compact crossover, single body style, FWD standard with AWD optional on most trims (recorded msrp is the FWD price; AWD price in the note where the source gives it). Generations: 2010-2017 (2nd gen; 2016 facelift; trims L/LS/LT/LTZ), 2018-2024 (3rd gen; L/LS/LT/Premier, RS added and L dropped with the 2022 refresh), 2025-on (4th gen; LT/RS/Activ). The gasoline Equinox only - the Equinox EV is a separate model. MSRPs exclude destination except where a year note says the charge could not be determined (2018, 2019, 2026).

years.note: cars.com 'Starting MSRP' per configuration; the page does not state a destination charge (recorded null). The 3LT and 3LZ entries show $0 ('Ltd Avail') and are ignored.

trims.note: AWD $27,400. Published $27,195 incl. destination (was $26,995 with the $1,195 charge).

years.note: Refreshed 2022 model (L trim dropped, RS added, 2.0L turbo discontinued). Figures = published 'MSRP + DFC' minus $1,395; the May-2022 step raised only the destination charge ($1,195 to $1,395), so the base MSRPs equal the launch level. GM Authority also reports 'another price increase' for 2022 in July 2022 (not fetched; amount unknown).
Figures = published 'MSRP + DFC' minus $1,395 (LS FWD $27,995, LS AWD $29,595, LT FWD $29,095, LT AWD $30,695, RS FWD $32,095, RS AWD $33,695, Premier FWD $33,195, Premier AWD $34,795).

trims.note: AWD $32,550. Up $250. thetruthaboutcars.com confirms the 2024 RS FWD 'stickered at $32,345' with AWD +$1,600.

years.note: Last year of the third generation (LS/LT/RS/Premier; 2025 is the all-new fourth generation with LT/RS/Activ). Figures = published 'MSRP + DFC' minus $1,395 (LS FWD $27,995, LS AWD $29,595, LT FWD $30,890, LT AWD $32,490, RS FWD $32,345, RS AWD $33,945, Premier FWD $33,195, Premier AWD $34,795).

trims.note: AWD $35,000. New trim for 2025. Published $34,395 incl. destination.

years.note: All-new fourth generation (first year): lineup cut to LT, RS and Activ (LS/Premier dropped). Published prices (LT FWD $29,995, LT AWD $31,995, RS/Activ FWD $34,395, RS/Activ AWD $36,395) include a $1,395 destination charge, 'the same as that for the 2024 model'; recorded MSRPs subtract it. Corroborated by thetruthaboutcars.com (Apr 30, 2024): starts at $29,995, RS and Activ $34,395, '$2,000 dearer' than the 2024 LS.

gaps: 2018, 2019, 2026: the only figures found were destination-inclusive (or of unstated basis), so they are left out of the table rather than recorded under 'MSRP excl. destination'; the engine uses its typical estimate for those years.
2016: no pricing page reached (blog.consumerguide.com 2016 facelift preview carries no prices; search budget exhausted).
2018: prices are destination-inclusive because no fetched page states the 2018 destination charge.
2019: TrueCar figures only; basis (incl./excl. destination) not stated by the page.
2020: destination charge not stated by cars.com (GM Authority's May-2022 article says the charge was $1,195 'previously', but does not tie that to 2020).

2022: a second 2022 increase (July 2022, GM Authority) was not fetched; the recorded level is after the May-2022 destination increase only. On these sources the 2022 LS/LT MSRPs ($25,800/$26,900) sit BELOW the 2020 cars.com figures ($26,300/$27,500) - looks like a repositioning with the refresh, not verified.
2024: LT rose $1,795 over 2023 while LS/Premier were unchanged - flagged as unusual, taken as printed.
2026: only the LT AWD price (destination-inclusive) was found on news.gm.com.

GM's own pricing pages (media.chevrolet.com, incl. the Jan-2024 2025 Equinox release) are robots-disallowed; gmauthority.com's 2025 options/packages article and aol.com's 2025 pricing article returned client errors.
